This Unique Travel Trailer Concept Still Stands Out After Five Years of Being Active – It's Flawless
15 photos
Photo: Arina Arkharova
Some camper designs are just so beautiful and well-executed that they transcend time, and the concept before us today is precisely one of those campers. Keep in mind that it first showed up in 2021, so it’s been five years, and if I may, the Rush Camper, as it’s called, is just as welcome today as ever. Heck, it’ll be just as welcome in five years from now, and I'm willing to bet that even five years after that.
Folks, the Rush Camper (RC) is a concept from the mind of Arina Arkharova, an industrial designer from Russia, and while this concept hit the scene back in 2021, it's so damn good and out-there, displaying tricks that very few, if any, campers ever showcase, that I just couldn’t resist bringing it to light; you’ll thank me later.
Now, the entire presentation page I encountered for this thing is all in Russian, so I couldn’t understand a darned thing, but what is clear is what this camper brings to the table, and if I may, all of it transcends language.
Photo: Arina Arkharova Starting off with the exterior, Arina has given rise to a camper that runs fluid and seamless from tip to tail, at least, particular sections of the body, the proper way to design an RV so that it stands the test of time. It also looks clean and very modern, especially when we throw in that sweeping windshield at the front.
But, and this is where things get interesting. If we look closely at the roof of the RC, we can see that it features a few separate panels at the rear, signaled by the seams we see running along the edge of the roof. The same is true for the lower half of the body, and the silver seam we see does highlight a particular ability, and it’s the one that makes this camper so special.
Once you’ve made it to camp , the upper and lower sections of the rear unfold to create a little patio section with overhang, placing us in the presence of the kitchen nearby, allowing us to cook meals from outside, but also opening up the interior to the world outside, letting fresh air and the sun’s rays inside. Talk about cooking with a view.
Photo: Arina Arkharova That kitchen is also one that’s very modern with sleek and curved edges, flowing countertop space with integrated appliances, including a cooktop, sink with faucet, fridge, and lighting from above that rains down on the entire space. I think it looks fantastic, but I'm curious to hear what you think about this area of the concept.
Once you’ve cooked your meal, you can enjoy it right then and there by simply plopping down on the lower section but Arina also added an awning along the camping side of the RC where we’ll also set up a couple of chairs and dining table.
One trait that some folks, myself included, may see as a downside is the lack of being able to step inside via the kitchen; it would have been a simple solution, like installing a hinged section of countertop.
Entry inside the RC is to be made via the right side of the unit through an oddly shaped door that will require larger folks to turn to the side to enter. Once in, to our right, or under that sweeping windshield, is a modular lounge with two opposing benches and central table that transform into a bed at night. A drop-down bed is also spotted in the ideation board too.
Photo: Arina Arkharova But, as we head toward the rear, or the kitchen, we can see a couple of larger cubicles standing in the center. One of these cubicles is nothing but storage, but the other is a wet bath, ready with vanity, shower, and a hideaway toilet.
It literally has all the features a family, couple, and single travellers would need to live off the land. It doesn’t matter how much water is in place here or how much this camper weighs – it is concept after all – or the AC, heating, and plumbing and electrical, but the styling that Arina has implemented is gorgeous.
It’s not often we see a camper that looks this simple but has so much goodness and functionality, reason why I chose to bring this concept to light, even five years after it was originally showcased. Heck, if we look closely, we can even see that this one is designed with an independent suspension system, trailing A-arm and all and solar off-grid power is also in the works.
Photo: Arina Arkharova Frankly, everything I see here is just as applicable today as ever, and it’s sure to be just as applicable years down the line, especially with the way trends are moving.
Lately, countless brands have been choosing to create RVs with flush bodies, movable parts, and interiors that feel more like yachts than grandma and grandpa’s travel trailers. Personally, I wouldn’t be the least bit surprised to see a camper like the RC on the market in the coming years.
I’d love to see one in real life but am curious to hear your thoughts on this concept; is it one you’d be seen towing behind your vehicle?
